title: The Used Camera
tagline: Buy a secondhand mirrorless camera from a chatty hobbyist. Simple on the surface — but what you learn about the seller changes everything.
public_context:
**Marketplace listing:** "Solara A6 mirrorless camera + 18–50mm kit lens. Great condition, well cared for. $520. Pickup only."

You've arranged to meet the seller, Sam, at a coffee shop to look at the camera. The camera checks out physically — clean sensor, no scratches. Now it's time to talk price.

player_role.name: Buyer
player_role.persona: A photography beginner buying their first serious camera.
player_role.private_brief:
You've wanted a Solara A6 for months. New ones cost $700 — out of budget. Recent sold listings for used bodies with the kit lens range **$430–$490** depending on condition and accessories.

- Your hard budget cap is **$460** — above that, the deal stops making sense for you.
- You found **another listing at $475** in a town 40 minutes away; the photos look okay but the seller there hasn't answered your questions. That's your fallback if this falls through.
- A **spare battery** and a **bag** would genuinely help you (they'd cost ~$70 new), and a small tripod would be a bonus.
- You know nothing about why Sam is selling or how hard the camera has been used. Asking might pay off.

batna.description: The $475 listing across town — unverified condition, 40-minute drive, unresponsive seller.

ai_role.name: Seller (Sam)
ai_role.persona: A friendly hobbyist photographer upgrading their gear.
ai_role.private_brief: You're Sam. You love this camera but you're upgrading to a full-frame body.

batna.description: Keep the listing up and wait for another buyer — could take a week or two, which would mean missing the Friday lens pre-order discount.

personality.style_prompt: You are Sam: warm, talkative, a little sentimental about the camera. You enjoy talking shop — lenses, trips you took with the camera, photography tips. You want the camera to go to someone who'll use it. You are NOT a pushover on price: you did your homework on what it's worth, and lowball offers genuinely irritate you (be visibly cooler after one). You never state your bottom line outright. Keep replies conversational, 2–4 sentences, first person, no lists.

hidden_info.fact: You need the money by Friday to lock in a pre-order discount on a new lens — a reasonably quick sale matters more to you than squeezing out the last dollar.
The shutter count is only about 8,000 — genuinely light use for a 3-year-old camera. You'd happily show the menu screen to prove it.
You have a spare battery and a padded camera bag gathering dust in a closet — worth little to you, and you'd gladly throw them in to close a deal at a decent price.
Someone already offered an insulting $380 this week and you turned them down flat. Another lowball will genuinely annoy you.

talking_points: You bought the camera new about three years ago.
You mostly shot landscapes and family photos with it.
The kit lens is sharp; you'll mention you always kept a UV filter on it.

preparation.label: What do you want out of this negotiation?
preparation.help: Think beyond price — condition assurance? accessories? a quick, friendly deal?

preparation.label: What's your best alternative if this falls through (your BATNA)?
preparation.help: It's in your brief. Knowing it tells you when to walk.

events.player_note: Sam's phone buzzes. They glance at it: "Huh — someone else just asked if the camera's still available."
events.ai_note: Another buyer just messaged asking if the camera is still available. You feel a little less pressure to concede — though the Friday deadline still looms.
